procedure: EA-NEGONT-02 v0.7 §3.4 D/R/O (working; not frozen). Admission by reading: a candidate is admitted to a stratum when its sentence or paragraph makes a claim of that stratum's kind: D, a claim on what the technological singularity is, how its literature stands, or whether and how it may occur; R, a relation between the technological singularity and an archive object (The Final Time and its stand-on sources, the archive's machine-dialectic line); O, an archive category applied to it (contingent singularity, terminal closure, terminal reflexivity, competing contingent Omegas, diminishing dialectic, the final time). Naming the word is not enough; most hits use 'singularity' in another sense. Machine compositions quoted in deposits are reception evidence and are not admitted. Volume is never a ground of removal; instances of one work are grouped as a lineage and kept.

verdicts.reason: The archive's defining paper on the entity (v0.5 as minted, text cut at §36.3), read whole. D: reads the technological singularity as a theory of runaway intelligence and the singularity literature as coordinates (Good, Vinge, Kurzweil, Chalmers, Bostrom, Modis, Thorstad), a family of hypotheses; §31 sets the two singularities side by side; §32 holds intelligence growth not decisive; §36.1 predicts intelligence explosion neither necessary nor sufficient, with a counterexample specified. O: contingent singularity, terminal closure, terminal reflexivity, competing contingent Omegas, diminishing dialectic, the final time as a viability boundary. R: Walt, Tiger Leap, Phase X, Monetary Dark Matter and Transition in Entropic Systems as the paper's stand-on sources.

Adds what #1635's cut omitted: §36.4–36.6 (incl. the two falsification tests), §37 non-claims (a technological singularity is not claimed impossible; the present decade is not claimed the final time), §38 (the singularity cannot be merely computational or symbolic; the positive singularity), Appendix B on the singularity literature (Vinge's routes through a system, Kurzweil's 'singularity' as metaphor, the contested family-resemblance term). Claims shared with #1635 are ledgered from #1635 as the earliest instance; #1637 instances are kept in the lineages.

Read in its entry 17 (Inversion) and the related entries: the archive's own one-sentence statement of the paper's thesis on the entity ('In The Final Time the singularity is a point of closure ... It rereads the technological singularity as an end of history, in the bad sense'). It states the thesis as closure; the paper defines a double singularity. The two are carried as contested within the pool.
